mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Real Final Sales of Goods signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines > 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a slowing economy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3% and GDPC1 YoY < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When Real Final Sales of Goods (RSAFS) increase by more than 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% within a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand and labor market tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
regime_hint: strong demand and labor market tightening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS increases > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months.
